theory.intro: A **scatter plot** shows bivariate data on the Cartesian plane. Each observation gives one point $(x, y)$, where $x$ is its independent-variable value and $y$ its dependent-variable value. The pattern the points form shows the relationship.
facts: Each observation contributes **one point** $(x, y)$: $x$ is its horizontal-axis value and $y$ its vertical-axis value. Identical data pairs overlap.
Choose an axis scale that fits the full range of the data. Starting near the data can help keep the points readable.
When helpful, a scale that starts near the data keeps the points spread out and readable.
**Label both axes** with the variable name and its units.
steps: Choose a scale for each axis that covers the full range of that variable's values.
Label both axes with the variable name and units.
Plot each data pair as a point at $(x, y)$.
Check that every data pair has been plotted. Identical pairs overlap, so the number of visible dots need not equal the number of observations.

mastery.question_text:
The table shows the height and arm span of $8$ students.
$\begin{array}{c|cccccccc} \text{Student} & \text{Amir} & \text{Bea} & \text{Cody} & \text{Dina} & \text{Ezra} & \text{Farah} & \text{Gia} & \text{Hugo} \\ \hline \text{Height (cm)} & 150 & 155 & 160 & 165 & 170 & 175 & 180 & 185 \\ \text{Arm span (cm)} & 145 & 160 & 155 & 170 & 165 & 180 & 175 & 190 \end{array}$
Choose a suitable scale for each axis, label both axes, and plot the data as a scatter plot.

The table shows the height and arm span of $8$ students.
$\begin{array}{c|cccccccc} \text{Student} & A & B & C & D & E & F & G & H \\ \hline \text{Height (cm)} & 151 & 158 & 163 & 168 & 168 & 176 & 183 & 189 \\ \text{Arm span (cm)} & 147 & 162 & 157 & 171 & 179 & 181 & 176 & 193 \end{array}$
Choose a suitable scale for each axis, label both axes, and plot the data as a scatter plot, with height on the horizontal axis.
